title: The Quiet Revolution in U.S.-Cypriot Relations
gist: Makovsky and Brody argue that over the past decade the Republic of Cyprus has turned itself from a 'problem to be solved' into a U.S. security producer, through basing upgrades, port calls, evacuation hubs, and training. Cyprus started this shift, and the souring of U.S.-Turkey relations accelerated it. Its risks are Turkish backlash, entanglement in the Israel-Iran conflicts, and possible U.S. abandonment.

insights.claim: Over the past decade, Cyprus has repositioned itself from a problem the United States wanted solved into a critical security partner. Cooperation now covers defense, trade, basing, training and exercises, crisis response, and regular strategic dialogue, and the impetus came from Nicosia rather than Washington.
insights.speaker: Alan Makovsky, Jonah Brody
insights.so_what: A new Eastern Mediterranean security node is forming, and it bears on regional energy and shipping security.
insights.quote: Cyprus is emerging as a security producer for the United States and the West

insights.claim: The pivot began in 2013, when pro-Western Nicos Anastasiades replaced the Moscow-friendly, anti-NATO communist Demetris Christofias as president. Anastasiades pitched Washington on Cyprus's ports, airfields, offshore energy resources, and location between Europe and the Middle East.
insights.speaker: Alan Makovsky, Jonah Brody
insights.so_what: Offshore energy was part of the pitch, so Cypriot gas development is tied to the US security relationship.

insights.claim: U.S. policy moved step by step: Biden called it a 'strategic partnership' in 2014, a 2018 bilateral statement of intent followed, and the 2019 Eastern Mediterranean Security and Energy Partnership Act declared Cyprus a 'key strategic partner' and opened a path to suspending the 1987 U.S. arms embargo.

entities: Eastern Mediterranean Security and Energy Partnership Act
insights.so_what: Legislative backing makes the partnership less dependent on which administration is in office.

Wess Mitchell, seen as the chief architect of the shift, testified in 2018 that the United States had wrongly treated the Eastern Mediterranean as settled terrain anchored by Turkey. He called it an 'emerging maritime frontier' and saw Greece and Cyprus as a hedge against an increasingly erratic Turkey.

insights.so_what: This framework still guides US Eastern Mediterranean policy, with Greece and Cyprus serving as a hedge against Turkey.

insights.claim: Cyprus is the only EU member outside both NATO and the Partnership for Peace. President Nikos Christodoulides says he wants Cyprus in NATO, though Turkey's veto makes that nearly inconceivable without a settlement, and he presents U.S. cooperation as a way to bring the National Guard up to alliance standards.

insights.so_what: NATO membership is blocked by Turkey, so integration will run through bilateral US channels.

insights.claim: In 2025, through EUCOM, the United States funded a roughly $588,000 assessment to bring Andreas Papandreou Air Base up to NATO standards. It recommended a new heavy-lift apron and an expanded runway, which Cyprus will pay for.
insights.speaker: Alan Makovsky, Jonah Brody
insights.so_what: Infrastructure built for heavy airlift raises Cyprus's value as a regional staging point.

insights.claim: A new EUCOM-funded heliport at Evangelos Florakis Naval Base will take Chinook-type helicopters, and the Defense Ministry is studying an expansion to host eight large warships. Limassol has hosted 22 U.S. Navy vessels since 2022, 15 of them since 2024.
insights.speaker: Alan Makovsky, Jonah Brody
insights.so_what: US port-call frequency is accelerating, a measurable indicator of the US presence in the Eastern Mediterranean.
insights.quote: Limassol has become a routine U.S. Navy port of call, hosting 22 vessels since 2022, including 15 since 2024.

insights.claim: In December 2024, Congress made Cyprus eligible for U.S.-financed multilateral training, the only non-NATO, non-Partnership for Peace country with that status. Navy SEALs trained with the Cypriot navy's underwater team in 2021 and 2024, and the New Jersey National Guard has partnered with Cyprus since 2022.
insights.speaker: Alan Makovsky, Jonah Brody
insights.so_what: Cyprus has unique legal status for US training, which signals deepening institutional ties.

insights.claim: Cyprus serves as an evacuation and humanitarian hub. U.S. Marines and Ospreys deployed to Papandreou Air Base in 2024 for possible Lebanon evacuations, Cyprus was a transit point during the June 2025 Iran conflict, it has sent more than 37,000 metric tons of aid to Gaza, and its Larnaca security center had trained more than 2,000 officials from more than 20 countries by 2025.
insights.speaker: Alan Makovsky, Jonah Brody
insights.so_what: Cyprus's crisis-response role becomes more important whenever the Middle East escalates.

insights.claim: When Cyprus tried to field Russian S-300 missiles in 1997, Ankara threatened to bomb them, and Washington pushed Nicosia to send them to Greece. When Cyprus bought Israel's Barak MX system in 2024, Turkey warned of consequences but did not threaten military intervention. The authors credit the new U.S. security relationship, including a limited but consistent U.S. troop presence, as among the most important reasons.
insights.speaker: Alan Makovsky, Jonah Brody
insights.so_what: A US presence provides indirect deterrence, which lowers the tail risk of Turkey-Cyprus military escalation.

insights.claim: Turkey keeps an estimated 30,000-40,000 troops in the northern third of the island. That territory is the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, which only Turkey recognizes, and the ROC's main security concern remains a Turkish threat.
insights.speaker: Alan Makovsky, Jonah Brody
insights.so_what: A large Turkish force posture keeps the island's security risk alive.

insights.claim: Cyprus, Israel, and Greece hold regular summits and cooperate on energy. The United States has endorsed the triangle and since Trump's first term has sometimes joined it as the '3+1', which makes Turkey uneasy.
insights.speaker: Alan Makovsky, Jonah Brody
insights.so_what: The 3+1 energy and security alignment shapes Eastern Mediterranean gas development and pipeline politics.

insights.claim: Cyprus now hosts more arms than at any point in decades. Washington has yet to act on a Cypriot request for excess defense articles made more than a year ago, which suggests U.S. caution about destabilizing the island.
insights.speaker: Alan Makovsky, Jonah Brody
insights.so_what: Watch whether that request is approved; it would signal how much the US is willing to provoke Turkey.

insights.so_what: Turkish-Israeli friction is spreading geographically, which adds risk premium to Eastern Mediterranean assets.

insights.speaker: Alan Makovsky, Jonah Brody
insights.so_what: Spillover from the Iran conflict has reached Cyprus, a direct risk to its tourism, shipping, and energy assets.

insights.claim: Cyprus faces two opposite dangers: being drawn into U.S. operations staged from the island, or being abandoned by a more isolationist United States. Nicosia reiterated at the start of the Iran war that it does not allow foreign militaries to stage offensive operations from its territory.
insights.speaker: Alan Makovsky, Jonah Brody
insights.so_what: Cyprus's no-offensive-staging stance limits its usefulness to the US in Middle East wars.

insights.claim: The authors predict that if the prospect of reunification vanishes altogether, the strategic ambiguity that let the partnership deepen quietly will become harder to sustain. Washington would then have to weigh Cypriot opportunity against Turkish sensitivities more openly.
insights.speaker: Alan Makovsky, Jonah Brody
insights.so_what: The end of reunification talks would be a trigger for an open US-Turkey dispute over Cyprus.

insights.speaker: Alan Makovsky, Jonah Brody
insights.so_what: There is room for further US expansion on Cyprus if US-Turkey ties worsen.
